integrity.basis: Hilbert direct-sum triangle inequalities on each weaving block, self-adjoint operator quadratic-form order, and an exact one-index scalar sharpness witness.
critical_steps: Blockwise relative perturbation bounds both coefficient-vector norms by (1+sqrt K) times the other.
Sum of squared block inequalities yields the uniform frame-operator Loewner interval.
One scalar-index construction attains the extremal comparison factors on both sides.
The source frame bounds and order interval yield the two-sided uniform frame bounds and condition-number control.
integrity.quantifiers: Every finite m>=2, every finite/countable I, every real/complex Hilbert H, all source g-frames satisfying the stated all-subset condition for any K>=0, every partition and source column.
integrity.unproved_limits: No result for infinitely many source frames, weaker full-index-only perturbation hypotheses, or general Hilbert C*-modules.

limitations: Requires relative perturbation control on every index subset, not merely on the entire index set.
The result is for Hilbert-space g-frames with finite m; no Hilbert C*-module extension is claimed.
The sharp universal comparison factor may exceed a particular family's optimal spectral-distortion constant.

title: Sharp, family-size-free spectral equivalence for weavings of \(g\)-frames
